title: AI demand strains Asia's power and capital
lede: September's data centre news in Asia Pacific was dominated by the collision between surging AI demand and the physical limits of power, capital and regulation. OpenAI signed a multi-year compute deal with Nvidia-backed Firmus in Malaysia that lifted its contracted capacity past 900MW, while Nvidia-backed projects in Indonesia and Australia moved forward with multi-gigawatt ambitions. Alibaba unveiled a self-developed AI chip and a plan to exceed 20GW of data centre capacity by 2032, joining Huawei's push for domestic silicon alternatives. The build-out is testing infrastructure: Malaysia's regulator said data centres now consume nearly a tenth of national electricity, Thailand halted 49 projects pending new rules, and Sydney's grid operator warned that transmission capacity is largely committed. Capital is moving just as fast — KKR and Singtel completed their takeover of STT GDC, a BlackRock-IFM consortium entered exclusive talks on Stack's APAC portfolio at roughly US$25 billion, and Australian operators raised AU$35 billion, mostly in debt, in the first nine months of the year.

themes.heading: OpenAI anchors Malaysian AI compute
themes.narrative: OpenAI signed a multi-year agreement to lease dedicated AI compute from two Firmus AI Factory sites in Malaysia, a deal reported across several outlets that pushed the Nvidia-backed developer's contracted capacity beyond 900MW. The arrangement makes the US AI company the anchor customer for an Australian operator's Malaysian campuses and reflects how Southeast Asia is absorbing hyperscaler workloads. In Australia, Nvidia said it is working with local providers to bring 2GW of capacity online by 2027, and Bitdeer AI pre-sold the full 9.5MW of its Johor facility more than a year before energisation.

themes.heading: China pursues silicon self-sufficiency
themes.narrative: Alibaba unveiled an AI accelerator it called China's most powerful chip, alongside plans to train a model of 5 trillion to 10 trillion parameters and to exceed 20GW of global data centre capacity by 2032. The announcements framed chips, cloud and compute as a single platform strategy. Huawei, meanwhile, prepared its Ascend 960 and an 11-chip portfolio as Beijing's strongest challenge to Nvidia, though a shortage of high-bandwidth memory is lifting production costs for Chinese chipmakers.

themes.heading: Malaysia's power math tightens
themes.narrative: Malaysia's Energy Commission said data centres now account for nearly a tenth of the country's total electricity consumption, with demand expected to climb further by year-end. Developers are responding with self-supply: DayOne and utility TNB proposed up to 1.5GW of on-site generation and battery storage for a planned Selangor campus. The government said data centres made up 44 percent of total investment into Malaysia in the first half of 2026, as its task force weighed more than 40 proposals against energy, water and connectivity constraints.

themes.heading: Regulators push back on growth
themes.narrative: Thailand suspended construction on 49 data centre projects while it drafts new regulations on electricity consumption and community impact. Singapore tabled its Digital Infrastructure Bill, promising existing facilities a transition period to meet energy-efficiency requirements. Nikkei reported that opposition to rapid data centre construction is spreading across Malaysia, Indonesia and India over power costs, water use and land, echoing resistance seen in other markets.

themes.heading: Capital rotates through platforms
themes.narrative: KKR and Singtel completed their joint takeover of STT GDC, one of Asia's largest data centre platforms, to fund AI-ready build-out. A BlackRock and IFM Investors-backed consortium entered exclusive negotiations to buy Stack Infrastructure's APAC portfolio for around US$25 billion, after Macquarie declined to bid. Blackstone's AirTrunk sought a S$2 billion loan ahead of a possible Singapore listing, while Zankore signed a US$3.1 billion facility — one of Asia's largest GPU-backed loans — for a planned 1GW AI factory in Indonesia.

themes.heading: Australia scrambles for capacity
themes.narrative: Transgrid said more than 20GW of data centre connection enquiries are in its pipeline and that existing Sydney transmission capacity is largely committed, warning new projects face delays. Planning authorities nonetheless approved Amazon's AUD 2.17 billion, 235MW campus in western Sydney. NextDC raised AU$1.1 billion in convertible notes to fund expansion, part of a broader trend that saw Australian operators raise at least AU$35 billion in 2026, 85 percent of it debt, according to Reserve Bank of Australia analysis.
